..
Issued at 129 AM CST Mon Nov 9 2026

Through next weekend (Sunday)...

Today: GOES East water vapor and RAP analysis indicate southwest US 
upper low centered in west TX along the International Border and Rio 
Grande Valley. This continues to keep broad isentropic ascent and 
cirrus deck draped across the ArkLaTex to Gulf Coast states. 
Temperatures are currently in the mid to upper 40s along and south 
of Interstate 20 while falling into the upper 30s to the north. 
Surface high is centered over the ArkLaTex into the Gulf Coast 
region, which will help gradient winds to decouple and become light 
to calm overnight. Seasonably cool lows remain on tap this morning 
(35F to 45F this morning). The dry soil conditions continue to 
support overachieving of the nocturnal cooling processes. This 
favors efficient radiational cooling, but high clouds could 
complicate outgoing longwave radiation and effective cooling.
Patchy frost was observed this morning and additional pockets of
frost are possible this morning. Kept HWO as is, even if high 
clouds may constrict the frost potential a little further 
northeast into the Highway 82 and Highway 45 corridors more 
towards the Golden Triangle in northeast MS. Protect plants 
(covered or brought indoors) from the frost and pets and people 
from the cold temperatures.

This week into next weekend: Quiet and dry pattern, with clouds and 
the occasional rain shower will be the norm through midweek. As 
the upper low ejects northeast tomorrow, will open up into a 
weaker shortwave. There remains enough isentropic ascent for broad
cloudiness through mid to late week (Wednesday to 
Thursday).Temperatures moderate into the mid 70s to near 80 
degrees by midweek. Dry thermo profiles will climb as ascent and 
moist advection increase. Precipitable water (PWs) climb around 
half inch to around 1.1 to 1.3 inches around mid-week (Wednesday 
to Thursday). This will lead to some isolated rain showers. In 
addition, a stronger shortwave will dive southeast of the Plains 
into the Midwest, with a surface low and moving into the OH 
Valley. This will drive a front southeast. All of this being said,
this could lead to some low chance (15 to 30 percent)/isolated 
rain coverage north of Interstate 20 into the Highway 82 corridor.
Unfortunately, minimal rain totals, less than a tenth of an inch,
will make no dent in ongoing drought concerns and only continue to
worsen again. 

The synoptic pattern will become deeply amplified as another 
strong spoke of energy on the western periphery of the mean 
trough. This will drive reinforcing strong high pressure, around 
1025-1030mb, out of central Canada southward across the Great 
Lakes to MS Valley into the Gulf Coast. Friday and likely again on
Saturday, additional spokes of northern stream vorticity/shortwaves
rotate our way down the westward side of the long wave trough 
which further deepens the upper troughing and reinforces the 
suppressed, cool and dry weather. In fact, the pattern becomes so 
amplified that at 500 mb, guidance generally agrees it will be 
colder over portions of our area than in portions of far northern 
Canada with heights at that level sinking to 35 dam below 
climatological average. Surface high will weaken slightly but this
looks to be the most efficient cold and another round of likely 
frost and light freeze next weekend. Just prior, clear days and 
full sun strong combined with stout pressure gradient will favor 
deep mixing and potential increased wildfire danger around Friday.
Blended guidance probs of light freeze are ow to medium chance 
(15 to 50 percent) and medium to high chance (60 to 80 percentage)
north of Interstate 20, with low chance probs of falling below 
28F (10 to 30 percent). The growing season concerns will persist. 
The exact depth and orientation of the cold airmass introduces 
uncertainty--our area will be on the western edge of the coldest 
airmass meaning small shifts east or west could mean multiple 
degrees of difference in temperature. For that reason, will 
continue to monitor trends without formally issuing HWO products 
at this time.

The trend in temperatures for the week will the seasonable warmth
through mid week (Wednesday to Thursday) to seasonably cool, 
highs some 8 to 12F below (55F to 64F on Friday to Saturday) and 
lows some 12F to 15F below (28F to 34F Friday night and 30F to 38F
Saturday night). Some patchy frost and light freeze is possible 
Thursday night as well. /DC/86/
